title: The bottom quick bar on a gym's page and on the member site can be reached with the Tab key while it is hidden off screen
what: On a phone-width screen, the gym's web page and the member website have a bar at the bottom ('Become a member', 'Ask', 'Get the app'). When it is not wanted it is only slid below the screen. Its buttons stay in the Tab order and stay readable by a screen reader, so a keyboard or screen reader user lands on buttons that cannot be seen.
expected: While the bar is hidden, its buttons are skipped by the Tab key and by screen readers, as the gym-owner site already does with its own bar.
who: visitors who use a keyboard or a screen reader
how_often: every visit, before scrolling past the top
fix_line: Take the bar's buttons out of the Tab order and hide them from screen readers while the bar is off screen

title: On a gym's web page the keyboard focus ring is drawn in the gym's own colour, so it disappears on the gym-coloured signboard and bottom bar
what: The ring that shows which button the keyboard is on always uses the gym's chosen colour. The top signboard, the board headings and the bottom bar are painted in that same colour, so on 'Become a member', 'Ask' and the other signboard buttons the ring is the same colour as the background and cannot be seen.
expected: The focus ring always stands out from what is behind it, for example in the text colour on gym-coloured parts.
how_often: every time on the signboard and bottom bar
fix_line: Draw the focus ring in the signboard's text colour where the background is the gym's colour

title: On the gym-owner website the colour dots and the source numbers are too small to tap easily
what: The six round colour choices next to 'Type your gym's name' are 30 by 30 pixels, and the small source numbers after the big figures are 11-pixel links. Both are well under the usual 44-pixel finger size, so on a phone it is easy to hit the wrong one.
expected: Every tappable thing is at least about 44 pixels in each direction, or has that much tappable space around it.
how_often: every time they pick a colour or open a source
fix_line: Give the colour dots and the source numbers a bigger tappable area without changing how they look

title: On a tablet or small laptop, the gym's photos scroll sideways with no scroll bar or arrows, so most photos look missing
what: Between phone and full computer width, the gym's photos sit in one sideways row with the scroll bar hidden and no arrows. The only hint, 'N photos, swipe', means nothing with a mouse and is hidden from screen readers. A visitor with a mouse sees two photos and no sign that there are more.
expected: When photos scroll sideways, there is a visible way to move through them with a mouse or keyboard, such as arrows or a scroll bar.
who: visitors on a tablet or small laptop with a mouse
how_often: every visit at that screen width
fix_line: Show arrows or a thin scroll bar on the photo row when the screen is not a touch phone
